message.content:
ATP synthase (also called F₁F₀‑ATPase) is the enzyme complex that produces the bulk of the cell’s ATP in mitochondria. It sits in the inner mitochondrial membrane and uses the proton motive force generated by the electron transport chain to drive the synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate (Pi).  

**Key points**

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Location** | Inner mitochondrial membrane (F₀ part embedded in the membrane, F₁ part protrudes into the matrix). |
| **Energy source** | Proton gradient (ΔpH + ΔΨ) created by the electron transport chain. |
| **Mechanism** | Protons flow back into the matrix through the F₀ channel, causing the F₀ rotor to turn. This mechanical rotation drives conformational changes in the F₁ catalytic domain, sequentially converting ADP + Pi into ATP. |
| **Stoichiometry** | Roughly 3 protons per ATP synthesized (though exact numbers can vary). |
| **Regulation** | Activity is tightly coupled to the respiratory chain; it is inhibited when the proton gradient collapses (e.g., by uncouplers). |

In short, ATP synthase converts the electrochemical energy stored in the proton gradient into chemical energy stored in ATP, making it the central machine for cellular energy production in mitochondria.
